summary: The exact candidate fixes the shared Chat Completions/Responses routing defect: text-only requests on multimodal-capable checkpoints reuse already-produced prompt IDs, while real media, empty IDs, raw-string fallback, and token-first encoders retain required behavior.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: text-only multimodal routing returned rendered text instead of [11, 12, 13]. Image/video/audio and ordinary text-model boundaries behaved as expected.
Five candidate regression/boundary tests passed for text-only ID reuse, each media type, empty IDs, string fallback, and token-first media routing.
Four Responses endpoint tests passed, including text-only ID forwarding and actual-media routing.
All 140 Chat serving unit tests passed.
All 36 Responses serving unit tests passed.
A 100,000-token ID list was preserved by identity; image/video/audio/all-media, empty-ID, raw-string, Inkling, Kimi K3, and text-checkpoint boundaries all passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2 was visible, but the defect is CPU-side prompt routing before engine execution. The original Qwen3.5-122B CUDA TP4 hardware, weights, and topology were unavailable; an unrelated GPU smoke would not validate the eliminated encodes.

remaining_limitations: The original Qwen3.5-122B CUDA TP4 deployment, model weights, 100k-262k contexts, and production replay were unavailable, so the claimed TTFT percentages were not independently measured.
The prepared environment has one AMD Instinct MI350X with ROCm 7.2, not the original four-GPU CUDA architecture.
Deterministic tests prove prompt routing and avoidance of downstream string-only encode paths, not model semantic accuracy or distributed serving performance.
No native files changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
